candidate.answerReason: Three red balls constitute one quarter of the total, so there are 12 balls altogether and 9 white balls.

methods.label: Solve the probability proportion
methods.explanation: Let the total number of balls be \(n\). Then \(3/n=1/4\), giving \(n=12\). Therefore, there are \(12-3=9\) white balls.
methods.levelReason: The retained equation is a simple proportion with a positive total count, solvable using elementary proportion rules.

methods.label: Use four equal parts
methods.explanation: Since every ball is equally likely to be drawn, the red balls make up \(1/4\) of the total. View the total as four equal parts. The 3 red balls form one part, so each part has 3 balls. The other three parts are white, giving \(3\times3=9\) white balls.
methods.levelReason: This method uses unit fractions and elementary multiplication within the grade 9 probability setting.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is recovering a ball count from an equally likely probability. Both methods use equal likelihood and part-total relationships. The retained method solves a proportion; the alternative interprets one quarter as one of four equal parts and counts the three white parts.
